Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:10:1.english: She paints her eyelids - She puts kohl between her eyes so that [they] appear attractive.

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:10:2.english: Pokeset - She parts her hair this way and that.

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:10:3.english: And she passes serak [rouge] over her face - A certain pigment [applied] so that she will appear red.

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:10:4.english: They smear [a substance] on her lower face - in order to remove the hair below.

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:11:1.english: She would adorn herself - [With] adornments like these, as stated here.

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:11:2.english: In the presence of her daughter-in-law - For she was so old that she had a daughter-in-law, who is her son's wife.

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:11:3.english: They taught only - [Referring to] that which it says: "A woman may make her adornments."

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:11:4.hebrew: אלא ילדה - בחורה שדרכה בכך, ולהכי הוי לה שמחה במועד:
Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:11:4.english: Only a young woman - A young woman whose way is [to do] so, and therefore it is a joy for her on the Festival.

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:11:5.hebrew: אבל זקינה לא - והיכי עבדא אשתך הכי, דמיקשטא? הא הויא זקינה:
Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:11:5.english: But [for] an old woman, no - And how does your wife do this, adorning herself? Behold, she is an old woman.

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:12:1.english: And even [if she is] standing at the entrance of her grave - she is permitted to adorn herself.

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:12:2.hebrew: לקל טבלא רהטא - פירוש: קשקוש הזוג, ר"ל מיני זמר בהילולא. וכי היכי דרהטא ילדה בת שית לקל הילולא, הכי עבדא בת שיתין, והכי נמי מיקשטא:
Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:12:2.english: At the sound of the timbrel she runs - Meaning: the ringing of the bell, that is to say, types of music at a wedding celebration. And just as a six-year-old girl runs at the sound of the celebration, so [too] does a sixty-year-old woman, and so too does she adorn herself.

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:13:1.hebrew: שניוול הוא לה - שגנאי הוא לה וניוול בסיד, ומצטערת בסיד:
Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:13:1.english: That it is a disfigurement to her - That it is a disgrace to her and a disfigurement with the lime, and she is distressed by the lime.

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:13:2.hebrew: שיכולה לקפלו במועד - אע"פ שהיא מנוולת בסיד:
Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:13:2.english: That she can peel off during the Festival - Even though she is made unattractive by the lime.

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:13:3.hebrew: שמחה היא לאחר זמן - במועד, לסוף המועד, לאחר שקפלתו את הסיד שטפלה, לפי שמשיר את השער ומעדן את הבשר. והואיל דהאי סיד משמחתה לאחר זמן, להכי שרי לה לטופלו במועד, אע"פ שהיא מצירה עכשיו:
Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:13:3.english: She will be happy afterward - During the Festival, [i.e.,] at the end of the Festival, after she has peeled off the lime that she applied, because it removes the hair and softens the flesh. And since this lime makes her happy afterward, therefore it is permitted for her to apply it during the Festival, even though she is distressed now.

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:14:1.hebrew: ומי אית ליה לרבי יהודה האי סברא - אע"ג שהיא מצירה עכשיו, שמחה וכו':
Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:14:1.english: And does Rabbi Yehuda hold this reasoning - Even though it distresses her now, [she will be] happy, etc.

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:15:1.hebrew: נפרעים מהם - מהכותים ביום חגם, מפני שהוא מצער, דכל אדם שפורע מיצר. אבל לא משלמים להם ממון ביום חגם, לפי שמשמחם ביום חגם ומודה לע"ז, כדפי' במס' ע"ז:
Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:15:1.english: One may collect from them - From the Cutheans on their festival day, because it causes [him] distress, for every person who pays [a debt] is distressed. However, one may not pay money to them on their festival day, because it makes them happy on their festival day and [thus] he gives thanks to idolatry, as I explained in Tractate Avodah Zarah.

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:15:2.hebrew: שמח הוא לאחר זמן - שפרע לו, ואמאי נפרע מהן? אבל לרבי יהודה לא אית ליה האי סברא, דמשום שמיצר עכשיו שרי. והיכי אית ליה האי סברא גבי טפול, אע"ג שהיא מצירה עכשיו, שמחה היא לאחר זמן:
Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:15:2.english: He is happy afterward - Because he paid him [off], so why should we collect from them? Whereas Rabbi Yehuda does not hold this reasoning, for because [the gentile] is distressed now, it is permitted. And how does he hold this reasoning regarding applying lime, [that] even though she is distressed now, she is happy afterward?

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:16:1.hebrew: הנח להלכות מועד - להכי א"ר יהודה הכא דשרי, אע"פ שהיא מצירה כו':
Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:16:1.english: Leave [aside] the halakhot of the Festival - For this reason Rabbi Yehuda says here that it is permitted, even though she is distressed, etc.

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:16:2.hebrew: דכולהו הלכות מועד - דשרי, משום האי טעמא נמי שרו, כגון אפיה ובישול, דמצער השתא כשהוא אופה ומבשל, ולהכי שרי דשמח הוא כשהוא אוכל אפייתו ובישולו ביו"ט:
Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:16:2.english: For all [the] laws of the Festival - that are permitted are also permitted for this reason — such as baking and cooking, where one is distressed now when he bakes and cooks, and therefore it is permitted, for he is happy when he eats what he baked and cooked on the Festival.

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:17:1.hebrew: כותי לעולם מיצר - שפורע, ולהכי לא אית ליה לר' יהודה התם אע"פ שמיצר שמח וכו'. אבל לעיל גבי טפול, אית ליה לר' יהודה אע"פ שמצירה עכשיו שמחה לאחר זמן:
Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:17:1.english: A Cuthean [gentile] is always distressed - When he repays [a debt]. Therefore, Rabbi Yehuda does not hold there [the principle of] "even though he is distressed [now], he is happy [later]," etc. However, above regarding applying cosmetic paste, Rabbi Yehuda holds [that] "even though it distresses her now, she is happy later."

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:18:1.english: Who reached their maturity - [To the stage of] hair.

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:18:2.hebrew: ולא הגיעו לשנים - שאינן בנות י"ב שנה ויום אחד, שעדיין אינו דין שיהא להן שער, ובושות על כך:
Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:18:2.english: And had not reached the years [of majority] - That they are not [yet] twelve years and one day old, for it is not yet normal for them to have hair, and they are embarrassed about this.

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:18:3.english: The poor smear - [they smear] the hair with lime and cause them [the hairs] to fall out.

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:1:1.hebrew: ובמצוה שא"א לעשותה ע"י אחרים - אל תפלס, אלא מצוה שבא לידך, בין גדולה בין קטנה, עשה:
Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:1:1.english: And regarding a mitzvah that cannot be done by others - Do not weigh [its importance]; rather, [any] mitzvah that comes to your hand, whether great or small, perform [it].

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:20:1.hebrew: אנפיקינון - היינו אנפיקינון דקתני התם במנחות (דף פה:), אנפיקינון לא יביא, היינו אותו שמן שעושין מזיתים:
Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:20:1.english: Anpikinon - This is [the same] anpikinon that is taught there in Menachot (85b): "[One] shall not bring anpikinon" — that is, the oil that they make from olives.

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:20:2.english: That have not reached a third [of their growth] - That [the olives] have not ripened a third.

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:20:3.hebrew: ולמה סכין אותו - אכל הני קא מהדר, דקאמר טופלין כו':
Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:20:3.english: And why do they smear it - It refers back to all of these [substances], where it said "they smear," etc.

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:21:1.english: And he took four hundred zuz for her - For she became beautiful, and he took that [amount] from her husband.

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:21:2.hebrew: טפלה כולה בחד זימנא - דסבר למיעבד כרב ביבי, ומתה:
Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:21:2.english: He smeared all of her at one time - For he thought to do as Rav Bivi [did], and she died.

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:21:3.english: Our daughters require smearing [with lime] - For beer causes hair to grow and thickens the flesh.

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:2:1.english: And all of your desires are not to be compared to her - [Meaning] that you should set aside all your desires in order to engage in Torah.

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:2:2.hebrew: חפצי שמים ישוו בה - כלומר, שאם יש לך לעסוק במצוה, תבטל תלמוד תורה ועסוק במצוה:
Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:2:2.english: Desires of Heaven can be compared to her - That is to say, if you have [occasion] to engage in a mitzvah, suspend Torah study and engage in the mitzvah.

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:2:3.english: That even desires of Heaven [are] not - That one sets aside a mitzvah and engages in Torah study.

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:4:1.hebrew: תעייל ולא תיפוק תיפוק ולא תעייל - משמע ליה בסחורה: תעייל ולא תיפוק — שתביא סחורה ולא תמכרנה; תיפוק ולא תעייל — שתוציא בסחורה במקום אחר ולא תביאנה:
Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:4:1.english: That you should bring in and not take out, that you should take out and not bring in - He understood it [as referring] to merchandise: "that you should bring in and not take out" — that you should bring in merchandise and not sell it; "that you should take out and not bring in" — that you should take out [money] for merchandise in another place and not bring it [in].

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:4:2.english: You shall bring in a bride - For [it is] the way of a bride to go to [her] husband.

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:4:3.hebrew: ולא תיפוק - דלא לימות בנך, דהדרי נפקי מינך והדרי לבי נשייהו:
Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:4:3.english: And not take out - That your son should not die, [whereby] they [your daughters-in-law] would go back out from you and return to their fathers' houses.

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:4:4.hebrew: שתא חדתא - זו שנה ראשונה של נישואין, דכתיב: "כי יקח איש אשה חדשה לא יצא וגו'" (דברים כ״ד:ה׳):
Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:4:4.english: A new year - This [refers to] the first year of marriage, as it is written: "When a man takes a new wife, he shall not go out, etc." (Deuteronomy 24:5).

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:6:1.hebrew: ליחרב ביתך - בית קברתך, דלא תמות אלא תחיה לאורך ימים:
Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:6:1.english: Your house should be destroyed - Your burial place, [meaning] that you shall not die, rather you shall live for a length of days.

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:8:1.hebrew: לא תבוש ולא תתבייש - לא תיבוש אחריני, כדי שלא תתבייש, שלא תבא לידי כך פן תתבייש:
Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:8:1.english: You should not shame and you should not be shamed - You should not shame others, so that you will not be shamed — that you should not come to such [a pass] lest you be shamed.

Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:9:1.hebrew: ותנא בה - ושנה בה "לא יבושו עמי לעולם", והיינו "לא תבייש ולא תתבייש":
Rashi on Moed Katan 9b:9:1.english: And repeated in it - And He repeated in it, "My people shall never be ashamed," and this is [what Rav meant by], "May you neither put [others] to shame nor be put to shame."

Tosafot on Moed Katan 9b:10:1.hebrew: פוקסת - פי' בקונטרס: מתקנת שער שלא יתפזר. וקשה, דבפרק המצניע (שבת דף צד: ושם) אמר דמתחייב בשבת משום טוה. ועוד, ד"סורקת" ה"ל למיתני, כמו גבי נזיר (נזיר מב.). ובפ' קמא דכתובות (דף ד: ושם) פירש בקונטרס: קליעת שער. וקשיא, דבפרק המצניע שונה "גודלת ופוקסת". ואין לפרש "מעברת סרק על פניה", דהכא תני תרוייהו, וגם בפ'. קמא דכתובות. ויש לפרש דמתקנת שערה בידיה חוץ לצעיף. וריב"א מפרש: שנותנת חוטין של בצק [דקין] על פניה להאדים הבשר, והיינו טוייה; והאי דקורא ליה בירושלמי "צובע", שהוא מאדים הבשר. ובנין נמי שייך בתיקון האשה, למאי דמפורש סוף המצניע (שבת דף צה.) משום בונה, ומייתי קרא ד"ויבן את הצלע":
Tosafot on Moed Katan 9b:10:1.english: Pokeset - Rashi explained: She arranges [her] hair so that it does not scatter. And this is difficult, because in the chapter HaMatzni'a (Shabbat 94b and there [in the parallel]), it says that one is liable on Shabbat [for this act] on account of spinning. Furthermore, it should have taught "combing" (soreket), as [it does] regarding a nazirite (Nazir 42a). And in the first chapter of Ketubot (4b and there), Rashi explained [pokeset as] braiding hair. And this is [also] difficult, because in the chapter HaMatzni'a it teaches "braiding (godelet) and pokeset" [as two distinct acts]. And one cannot explain [pokeset as] applying rouge to her face, because here [in our baraita] it teaches both of them, and also in the first chapter of Ketubot. Rather, one can explain that she arranges her hair with her hands outside her veil. And Riba explains: That she places [thin] threads of dough on her face to redden the flesh, and that is [why it is considered] spinning; and that which the Yerushalmi calls it "dyeing" is because it reddens the flesh. And "building" also applies to a woman's adornment, according to what is explained at the end of HaMatzni'a (Shabbat 95a), [that she is liable] on account of "building," and it cites the verse, "And He built the rib" [Genesis 2:22].

Tosafot on Moed Katan 9b:19:1.hebrew: סטכת - בפרק כל הקרבנות (מנחות דף פו.) מפרש דשמן המור הוא סטכת, ובפ' קמא דמגילה (דף יג.): "מאי שמן המור? רב הונא אמר רבי חייא: סטכת":
Tosafot on Moed Katan 9b:19:1.english: Setaket - In the chapter [entitled] Kol HaKorbanot (Menachot 86a), [the Gemara] explains that shemen hamor is setaket. And in the first chapter of Megillah (13a) [it states]: "What is shemen hamor? Rav Huna said [in the name of] Rabbi Ḥiyya: Setaket."

Tosafot on Moed Katan 9b:3:1.hebrew: כאן במצוה שאי אפשר לעשותה ע"י אחרים - עשיית מצוה עדיף, שהרי מפסיקין אפילו לר"ש בן יוחי לעושה סוכה ולולב, כדאי' בירושלמי. אבל בהפסקה דתפלה וק"ש, אין מפסיקין לר"ש בן יוחי; ובירושלמי: "זה שננו וזה שננו, ואין מפסיקין שננו מפני שננו":
Tosafot on Moed Katan 9b:3:1.english: Here, [it is referring to] a mitzvah that cannot be performed by others - Performing the mitzvah is preferable, for one interrupts [Torah study] even according to Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai for one making a sukkah and a lulav, as is stated in the Yerushalmi. However, regarding interrupting for prayer and the recitation of the Shema, one does not interrupt according to Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai; and in the Yerushalmi [it states]: "This is our study and this is our study, and we do not interrupt our study for our study."
